metadata.title: ProductLens AI
metadata.voice_note: Synthetic local Kokoro voice reading Aditya's script in first person (disclosed in SOURCES.md).
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Course pitch film (INFO7375 final project pitch, 2–4 min): opens on the hesitant writer, no terms card, no verdict card and no Your Turn beat; runtime goes to the seven required pitch answers. Spoken outro stays.
metadata.audience: INFO7375 instructor and TAs; hiring managers for AI product manager roles
metadata.honesty: Past tense only for what exists. Drawings of the unbuilt product tagged 'constructed'; Aditya's real run tagged.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Aditya Hasija. Product managers ask one question all the time: should we build this feature? I think a better question is: what should we test first?
beats.motion_claim: The writer types the usual question and corrects it to the better one.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Say you're a product manager at an online shoe store, and your team wants a one-page checkout.

shot.visual_intent: A kraft shopping cart; a four-step strip of checkout pages folds into one page.
shot.motion_claim: A kraft shopping cart; a four-step strip of checkout pages folds into one page.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Before you build it, you need to know what customers want, what other stores do, and what could go wrong. That research takes days, and a good-sounding idea isn't always a good decision.

shot.visual_intent: Three question cards rise in turn beside the folded page: customers, competitors, risks.
shot.motion_claim: Three question cards rise in turn beside the folded page: customers, competitors, risks.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: That's the job of my project, ProductLens AI. You type in the feature and the goal, say, more completed purchases, and attach a few public articles. It will give back a one-page decision brief.

shot.visual_intent: A feature card and two article pages slide into a dark machine; one brief page slides out.
shot.motion_claim: A feature card and two article pages slide into a dark machine; one brief page slides out.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: The brief will list the biggest risks, the numbers to watch, like checkout completion, and the first experiment to run. Every claim in it will be marked: backed by a source, or an assumption.

shot.visual_intent: The brief page is large: three section bars draw in; 'sourced' and 'assumption' tags land on lines.
shot.motion_claim: The brief page is large: three section bars draw in; 'sourced' and 'assumption' tags land on lines.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Inside, three AI agents will each take one angle: the market, the customers, and the risks. A fourth agent, the checker, compares their work to the sources and can send one back to fix it, once.

shot.visual_intent: The idea card splits to three agent blocks; their pages go to a review desk; one goes back once.
shot.motion_claim: The idea card splits to three agent blocks; their pages go to a review desk; one goes back once.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Can't a chatbot already do this? I tested it myself. On October 25th, I gave ChatGPT the shoe-store idea plus a made-up claim: Baymard, a checkout research firm, says one-page checkouts always convert better. Their research says it depends.

shot.visual_intent: Aditya's real ChatGPT screenshot (cropped to the conversation, date visible); the planted line is underlined.
shot.motion_claim: Aditya's real ChatGPT screenshot (cropped to the conversation, date visible); the planted line is underlined.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It caught my made-up claim right away, and the advice was solid. But only one paragraph had a source, and it rarely said which points were facts and which were guesses.

shot.visual_intent: The screenshot pans down; its one source chip is circled; unlabelled rows get grey '?' marks.
shot.motion_claim: The screenshot pans down; its one source chip is circled; unlabelled rows get grey '?' marks.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: That's the gap I'm aiming at. Tools like DimeADozen and ValidatorAI already score whole startup ideas. ProductLens is for one feature in a product that already exists, with every claim labelled and checked.

shot.visual_intent: A big 'startup idea' crate beside one small feature card that gets a 'sourced' tag and a check.
shot.motion_claim: A big 'startup idea' crate beside one small feature card that gets a 'sourced' tag and a check.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: When it's done, it will be a GitHub repository with the app, a set of made-up test ideas, and a score sheet.

shot.visual_intent: A release parcel opens: an app window, a fan of test cards, and a score sheet rise out.
shot.motion_claim: A release parcel opens: an app window, a fan of test cards, and a score sheet rise out.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: If you're hiring for an AI product role, you'd open it and, within a minute, see one sample brief and how often the checker caught planted mistakes, misses included.

shot.visual_intent: Three pages land on a desk in order (README, brief, scores); a cursor touches each.
shot.motion_claim: Three pages land on a desk in order (README, brief, scores); a cursor touches each.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It should show that I can write clear instructions an AI has to follow, check its answers against sources, and measure how well it works. It won't show I'm a machine learning engineer.

shot.visual_intent: An instruction page and a gate; the agent's answer must fit a dashed outline before the barrier lifts.
shot.motion_claim: An instruction page and a gate; the agent's answer must fit a dashed outline before the barrier lifts.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: The first step is small: one agent, one feature idea, run from the command line. You'll know it worked when it saves a log where every quoted source checks out.

shot.visual_intent: One parcel rides a short conveyor; a single log page drops out and a check draws on it.
shot.motion_claim: One parcel rides a short conveyor; a single log page drops out and a check draws on it.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: It won't plug into company data, run real A/B tests, or say go or no-go. It suggests the test; people decide.

shot.visual_intent: A card marked 'go / no-go' rides to a gate; the barrier drops and it slides away.
shot.motion_claim: A card marked 'go / no-go' rides to a gate; the barrier drops and it slides away.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: The biggest risk is a checker that agrees with everything, since it's the same AI grading its own team.

shot.visual_intent: A cracked page slides under an approval stamp; the stamp approves it anyway.
shot.motion_claim: A cracked page slides under an approval stamp; the stamp approves it anyway.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: So I'll hide mistakes in ten test ideas and count how many it catches. If it misses too many, those checks move into plain code.

shot.visual_intent: Test samples slide into a bench; a tally grows; a small code block docks beside it.
shot.motion_claim: Test samples slide into a bench; a tally grows; a small code block docks beside it.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: I changed this from my first pitch, a pre-mortem tool for startup ideas, because it was too close to an AI wrapper. I wanted something built for product managers, with real everyday use.

shot.visual_intent: Last pitch's idea crate shrinks away; the product-manager feature card takes its place.
shot.motion_claim: Last pitch's idea crate shrinks away; the product-manager feature card takes its place.

beats.narration_text: Why this project? It's a mix. I've spent years in product roles writing requirements and doing research, and my WorkShip, SkillPort and Touchline projects are on GitHub. Building and testing AI agents is the new part.

shot.visual_intent: A filled 'have' shelf beside an outlined 'new' shelf.
shot.motion_claim: A filled 'have' shelf beside an outlined 'new' shelf.

beats.narration_text: Today, ProductLens is a plan: the idea, a written outline, and my chatbot test. Everything else I'll build with Claude Code in the next two weeks.
